results.title: The Sound of music (Captioned)
results.creator_credit: Robert Wise, Argyle and Twentieth Century-Fox Film Corporation
results.brief_description: The Sound of music, the most popular movie musical of all time, is a heart warming, inspirational and true story based on the lives of the Trapp Family Singers. Julie Andrews is Maria, a spirited, young Austrian woman who becomes governess to the children of the autocratic widower Baron von Trapp (Christopher Plummer). She brings warmth and music to the strict household of the reserved former naval captain, and soon wins over the children - and finally the baron as well.

results.title: My fair lady (Captioned)
results.creator_credit: George Cukor, Jack L. Warner and Warner Bros Pictures
results.brief_description: The dazzling film version of Lerner and Loewe’s acclaimed musical. Audrey Hepburn stars as the cockney flowergirl Eliza Doolittle who is trained by Professor Higgins (Rex Harrison) to pass as a duchess. Featuring sumptuous cinematography and costumes by Cecil Beaton, this is one of the most popular musicals ever filmed. Winner of eight Academy Awards including Best Picture. The original musical is based on George Bernard Shaw’s “Pygmalion”.

results.title: Alien (Captioned)
results.creator_credit: Ridley Scott, Walter Hill, David Gilger, Gordon Carroll and Twentieth Century-Fox Film Corporation
results.brief_description: A sci-fi thriller with a difference. The crew aboard the space freighter Nostromo investigate a distress call and one of the crew brings back on board an Alien of unknown origin. In comparison to the technology dominated sterile world controlled by a computer, where no-one trusts anyone, the horror of the Alien is its very organic nature. Under Scott’s direction this film is grippingly suspenseful and draws interesting parallels between the perfect inhumanity of the Alien and that of the company. Stars Sigourney Weaver, Dean Stanton and John Hurt.

results.title: The African Queen (Captioned)
results.creator_credit: James Agee, John Huston, Sam Spiegel, Horizon (GB) and Horizon (US)
results.brief_description: Humphrey Bogart is the gin-soaked river tramp who reluctantly becomes a hero after rescuing a “skinny-psalm-singing-old-maid” (Katherine Hepburn) from the Germans during World War I. Their hazardous mission of escape becomes a pursuit as the odd pair survive malaria, insects, leeches and the persistent conflict of their personalities in order to destroy a German gunboat in the African Congo. Bogart won an Oscar for this role and the script was co-written by James Agee, based on C. S. Forester’s novel.

results.title: The Little princess (Captioned)
results.creator_credit: Walter Lang, Darryl F. Zanuck and Twentieth Century-Fox Film Corporation
results.brief_description: A charming story set in Victorian England stars Shirley Temple. When her widower father, an army officer, is sent off to the Boer War, Shirley is placed in a boarding school. When he is reported killed, the mean headmistress relegates Shirley to being a servant. She suffers her indignities bravely until her shell shocked father returns. The film contains a famous dream ballet in which Shirley is crowned a princess, plus several dazzling song and dance numbers performed with Arthur Treacher. Based on the novel by Frances Hodgson Burnett.

results.title: The Comancheros (Captioned)
results.creator_credit: Michael Curtiz, George Sherman and Twentieth Century-Fox Film Corporation
results.brief_description: A member of the legendary Texas Rangers works undercover to foil a notorious gang of outlaws in this top-notch Western. John Wayne stars as the two-fisted Ranger heading a cast that includes Stuart Whitman and Lee Marvin. The last film directed by Michael Curtiz “The Comancheros” is a lively, riotous Western with some exciting action sequences. Based on the novel by Paul I. Wellman.

results.title: The Barbarian and the geisha (Captioned)
results.creator_credit: John Huston, Eugene Frenke and Twentieth Century-Fox Film Corporation
results.brief_description: In 1856 American Governor Harris became the first foreign diplomat to visit the Forbidden Empire of Japan. This semi-historical romance stars John Wayne as the diplomat engaged in hostile trade talks with the Japanese government, who finds himself falling in love with a beautiful geisha. Huston has directed a finely crafted tale of adventure and intrigue. The production was filmed entirely in Japan.

results.title: The Littlest rebel (Captioned)
results.creator_credit: David Butler, B.G. De Sylva and Twentieth Century-Fox Film Corporation
results.brief_description: The troubles of the Civil War come home to a little plantation girl when her father is arrested and charged with espionage against the Yankees. Only a plea to President Lincoln can save the day. One of the most dramatically interesting of Shirley Temple’s films, “The Littlest Rebel” is also a spirited musical comedy featuring an exuberant performance by the gifted dancer, Bill “Bojangles” Robinson.

results.title: Before the revolution = Prima della rivoluzione
results.brief_description: Bertolucci’s second film, made at the preposterous age of 22, is a stunning examination of a young man caught between attraction for his bourgeois past and his faith in the revolutionary future of Marxism. Utilising an elliptical and experimental mise-en-scene, the film is a confident exploration of the movie medium. In formal setpieces, such as the film’s climax in a Parma Opera House, the film prefigures the distinctly personal cinema of spectacle that Bertolucci was to pioneer in the seventies. Inspired by Stendhal’s “The Charterhouse of Parma”, “Before the Revolution” is filled with literary, cinematic and political references reflecting the young director’s impatient and enthusiastic interrogation of his decaying class and society. The title comes from a quote by Talleyrand: “Only those who lived before the revolution know the sweetness of life.”
